key_insight: Mixing nanoscale Laponite with microscale Bentonite reduces drying damage, with composition and substrate influencing whether clay films remain intact, crack or peel.
engineering_relevance: Clay composition offers a simple route to improve drying resistance in coatings, barrier layers and ceramic processing.
method: Compare drying damage across clay compositions on hydrophobic polypropylene and hydrophilic glass.
Measure two-step yielding and derive step-dependent cohesive energies from gel rheology.
Use an energy-balance-derived cohesion–adhesion index to interpret cracking versus peeling.
evidence_signal: Replicate experiments found essentially intact Laponite films, extensive Bentonite fracture and, on glass, less damage for most intermediate compositions than a simple average would predict.
watch_item: Rheology–damage correlations must specify the yielding step used, because inferred cohesive energies differ by orders of magnitude.
paper_title: Resisting Drying Stress in Laponite Bentonite Clay Composites, Two Step Yielding and Crack Peel Selection
